newsitem.title: USA: SWIMMING-OLYMPIANS AMONG FIRST QUALIFIERS AT U.S. TRIALS.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-OLYMPIANS AMONG FIRST QUALIFIERS AT U.S. TRIALS.

text.p: The United States will have at least a few familiar faces at the world championships next January in Perth, Australia.

The first swimmers to qualify for the U.S. team Saturday night at the Phillips 66 U.S. national championships were 1996 Olympians Jenny Thompson, Amy Van Dyken, Kurt Grote, Jeremy Linn, Josh Davis and Brooke Bennett.
The top two finishers in each event qualify for the worlds January 8-18.
The seven-day meet is also serving as selection trials for the Pan Pacific Games in Japan August 10-13 and world university games August 25-30 in Sicily.
Thompson, 24, qualified in the 100-meter freestyle. Her morning preliminary time of 54.95 seconds was the fastest time swum in the world this year. She won in 54.96.

Van Dyken, 24, the top U.S. gold medal winner at the 1996 Olympics with four, was second in 55.66 and also qualified. Van Dyken said she will skip the Pan Pacifics to concentrate on her training for worlds.
"It will be nice to see what the rest of the world has in January," Van Dyken said. "It will be interesting to see how we stack up."
Grote, an Olympic silver medallist, won the 100-meter breaststroke in 1:01.45. Linn was second and also qualified.
Quance won the 400-meter individual medley in 4:39.67.
Davis, winner of four 1996 Olympic gold medals, won the 200-meter freestyle in 1:49.

Bennett, an Olympic 800 freestyle gold medallist, won the 1,500-meter freestyle in 16:10.93. She was attempting to become only the second woman to swim under 16 minutes. Three-time Olympian Janet Evans was the first.
